headline: A stray puppy walked in and hopped on a salesman’s lap: ‘We just fell in love’
author: Kyle Melnick

paragraphs.text: Salesman Roman Letsis was talking with a customer at his desk on a recent afternoon when a puppy walked into the car dealership’s open door.
The Great Pyrenees mix seemed to know exactly what she was looking for: She ran directly to Letsis’s desk and hopped onto his lap.
Letsis, 18, had never seen the dog before, but began petting her even though she was covered in dirt. The dog spent the rest of Letsis’s shift lounging next to him.
“Whose dog is this?” asked Josh Letsis, Roman’s father and the owner of Always Auto in Wichita Falls, Texas.
After Roman explained that the dog simply made herself at home, they took her to their house that Saturday night two weeks ago.
They planned to take the dog to a veterinarian and hoped they could either connect her with her owner or find her a new home.
“As the day transpired, we just fell in love with her a little more, a little more,” Josh said.

The puppy, whom Roman named Nova because he liked the sound of it, was lethargic and sick the following day. Josh and Roman said they couldn’t find a veterinary clinic open nearby but located an emergency office about 100 miles southeast in Denton, Texas.
“Let’s hop in the truck and just take her now,” Josh, 47, recalled telling his son. “Better be safe than sorry.”
Josh said that might have saved Nova’s life.

The puppy had a hookworm infection, and also parvovirus, a disease that can cause severe gastrointestinal illness and is typically fatal when untreated. The office didn’t find a microchip or tag on Nova, said Josh, who believes Nova was abandoned.
The veterinary bill was about $4,000. Josh said he couldn’t bear to leave Nova, who is about 6 months old, untreated. He paid for her care.
Nova got fluids, antibiotics, a plasma transfusion, and nausea and deworming medication, according to a discharge document from the clinic.
The office sent the family daily updates on Nova, who was fed through a tube at one point because she barely ate on her own, Josh said.
“For not knowing the dog very long, we felt very attached to her,” Josh said. “And we really felt like she was part of the family.”
Josh and Roman prayed for her recovery. Roman decided that if Nova survived, he would adopt her.
“It was kind of just a no-brainer,” Roman said. “I knew I wanted to make her my dog.”

The veterinary office told the family last week that the puppy was healthy and ready to be picked up. In the days since, Nova has been chewing on bone treats and a squirrel toy, and bulking up with chicken and rice.
Nova’s outgoing personality has emerged on visits to Always Auto, which repairs vehicles and sells used cars. The pup greets customers as they enter.
Since Wichita Falls news station KAUZ reported the story, Josh said some people have asked to visit the dealership just to meet Nova.
“It’ll be kind of fun having her as the mascot,” he said.
